title: Kaposi Sarcoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Kaposi Sarcoma (KS). Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (punch/excisional skin/mucosal biopsy with HHV-8 / LANA-1 IHC, HIV-1/2 screening, CD4 count, viral load, chest CT, fecal occult blood / endoscopy / bronchoscopy if symptomatic visceral involvement, KSHV-associated inflammatory cytokine syndrome KICS evaluation) -> Clinical Subtype Stratification (Classic/Mediterranean, Epidemic/HIV-associated, Endemic/African, Iatrogenic/Organ transplant-associated) -> ACTG Staging for HIV-KS (Good risk T0 I0 S0 vs Poor risk T1, I1, S1) -> Frontline Systemic Therapy: Optimize Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) for all HIV+ patients; Pegylated Liposomal Doxorubicin (sarc-kaposi-liposomal-doxorubicin Category 1 Preferred) for symptomatic, widespread, visceral, or rapidly progressive disease; Paclitaxel weekly (Category 1 Preferred) for advanced refractory; Local Therapy (intralesional vinblastine, topical alitretinoin, radiation therapy 20-30 Gy, surgical excision) for limited cutaneous disease; Second-line / Refractory: Pomalidomide, Lenalidomide, Gemcitabine, Etoposide; Iatrogenic KS management (calcineurin inhibitor reduction/switch to mTOR inhibitor Sirolimus). References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Kaposi Sarcoma Version 2.2026 (July 2026).

a.text: Definitive KS diagnosis requires tissue: 3-4 mm punch biopsy or incisional/excisional biopsy extending into subcutaneous fat. Histology shows slit-like vascular channels, spindle cells, extravasated red cells, and hemosiderin; nuclear HHV-8 / LANA-1 immunohistochemistry exceeds 99% sensitivity and specificity and distinguishes KS from mimics (bacillary angiomatosis, pyogenic granuloma, angiosarcoma).

b.text: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 2-3 weeks is the Category 1 preferred frontline systemic therapy for symptomatic, widespread, visceral, or rapidly progressive KS; weekly paclitaxel is the Category 1 preferred alternative, particularly for anthracycline-refractory or advanced disease.

c.text: Initiate or optimize antiretroviral therapy (ART) in every HIV-positive KS patient regardless of CD4 count or disease extent; ART alone can regress limited disease. Monitor for immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome KS flare (IRIS-KS) in the first months after ART initiation, especially with low baseline CD4, high viral load, or bulky disease.

d.text: In iatrogenic/transplant-associated KS, taper calcineurin inhibitors (cyclosporine, tacrolimus) wherever graft function permits and consider conversion to an mTOR inhibitor (sirolimus or everolimus), which combines immunosuppressive activity with direct anti-KS antineoplastic and antiangiogenic effects. Coordinate every change with the transplant team.

e.text: Screen KS patients for KSHV/HHV-8 syndromes: multicentric Castleman disease (MCD) and KSHV-associated inflammatory cytokine syndrome (KICS) with serum HHV-8 viral load, IL-6, IL-10, ferritin, CRP, CBC for cytopenias, and spleen assessment; MCD/KICS with concurrent KS needs co-management of both conditions.

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Kaposi Sarcoma: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete the diagnostic workup before subtype classification. Confirm tissue diagnosis with HHV-8 IHC, establish HIV/immune status, stage systemic and visceral extent, and screen for KSHV-associated syndromes.
bullets: Complete skin, oral mucosa, ocular, lymph node, and genital examination with photo documentation of sentinel lesions; record lesion count, size, morphology (patch, plaque, nodule), edema, ulceration, and bleeding.
Diagnostic tissue biopsy: 3-4 mm punch biopsy or incisional/excisional biopsy extending into subcutaneous fat; mucosal or nodal lesions biopsied by the least morbid adequate technique.

Pathology and IHC: slit-like vascular channels, spindle cells, extravasated red blood cells, hemosiderin deposition; HHV-8 / LANA-1 nuclear IHC exceeds 99% sensitivity and specificity; exclude bacillary angiomatosis, pyogenic granuloma, and angiosarcoma.

HIV and immunologic testing: HIV-1/2 serology; CD4 count and percentage; HIV RNA viral load; medication and transplant history for iatrogenic immunosuppression (calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids).

Systemic staging: chest radiography or contrast-enhanced chest CT; fecal occult blood testing (FOBT) with upper endoscopy/colonoscopy when gastrointestinal symptoms, bleeding, or anemia are present; bronchoscopy for respiratory symptoms, hemoptysis, or pulmonary infiltrates.

KSHV/HHV-8 syndrome screening: evaluate for multicentric Castleman disease (MCD) and KSHV-associated inflammatory cytokine syndrome (KICS) with serum HHV-8 viral load, IL-6, IL-10, ferritin, CRP, CBC for cytopenias, and spleen assessment for splenomegaly; co-manage MCD/KICS when present.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Clinical Subtype Classification

nodes.name: Clinical Subtype
nodes.title: Kaposi Sarcoma: Clinical Subtype Classification
nodes.description: Workup complete. Classify into one of the four epidemiologic/clinical KS subtypes; subtype plus extent determines local versus systemic therapy.
bullets: Epidemic / HIV-associated KS: HIV-positive patient, often with low CD4 count and detectable viremia; aggressive mucocutaneous and visceral pattern; stage with ACTG criteria (Tumor, Immune, Systemic: good risk T0 I0 S0 versus poor risk any T1, I1, or S1).

Classic / Mediterranean KS: typically older men of Mediterranean, Eastern European, or Middle Eastern descent; indolent violaceous plaques and nodules of the lower extremities with chronic lymphedema.
Endemic / African KS: HIV-negative African patients; ranges from indolent cutaneous disease to aggressive lymphadenopathic and visceral forms, including florid disease in children.

Iatrogenic / Transplant-associated KS: chronically immunosuppressed patients (solid-organ transplant on calcineurin inhibitors, prolonged corticosteroids); often regresses when immunosuppression is tapered or converted to mTOR inhibition.

nodes.name: HIV-KS Extent
nodes.title: Epidemic (HIV-Associated) KS: Disease Extent and ACTG Risk
nodes.description: Stratify HIV-associated KS by symptoms, cutaneous burden, edema, and visceral involvement, mapped to ACTG stage. Extent selects ART-alone/local versus ART-plus-systemic-chemotherapy pathways.
bullets: ACTG staging: Tumor (T0 confined to skin/minimal oral disease versus T1 tumor-associated edema, extensive oral, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, or other visceral involvement); Immune (I0 CD4 >= 150 cells/uL versus I1 CD4 < 150 cells/uL); Systemic (S0 no systemic illness versus S1 history of opportunistic infection, thrush, B symptoms, or poor performance status). Good risk is T0 I0 S0; poor risk is any T1, I1, or S1.
Limited disease: asymptomatic, limited cutaneous lesions without edema, ulceration, or visceral involvement; typically ACTG good risk (T0 I0 S0).

Advanced disease: symptomatic or extensive cutaneous disease, tumor-associated edema, ulcerated or bleeding lesions, pulmonary involvement (dyspnea, hemoptysis, infiltrates), or gastrointestinal involvement (bleeding, obstruction); generally ACTG poor risk (T1 and/or I1 and/or S1).

Refractory disease: progression on or within months of frontline pegylated liposomal doxorubicin despite optimized ART and adherence; confirm adherence, ART response (viral load, CD4 trend), and exclude IRIS-KS flare or MCD/KICS before relabeling as refractory.

options.label: Limited: asymptomatic limited cutaneous disease, no visceral involvement
Advanced: symptomatic, extensive cutaneous, edema, or visceral (pulmonary/GI) involvement
Refractory: progression on frontline liposomal anthracycline

nodes.name: HIV-KS Limited Treatment
nodes.title: HIV-KS, Limited: Optimize ART With Observation or Local Therapy
nodes.description: Immediate ART initiation or optimization is the backbone for limited HIV-associated KS; add local therapy only for cosmetically or functionally bothersome lesions.
bullets: Immediately initiate ART in treatment-naive patients or optimize the regimen with HIV specialist input in treatment-experienced patients (genotype resistance testing when viremia persists); ART alone induces regression of limited KS in a substantial proportion of patients.
Observe asymptomatic limited lesions once ART is optimized; reassess skin, mucosa, edema, CD4 count, and viral load every 4-8 weeks initially.

Local therapy for bothersome, bleeding, edematous, or cosmetically distressing lesions: intralesional vinblastine, topical alitretinoin 0.1% gel, low-dose radiotherapy (20-30 Gy), or surgical excision of isolated nodules.

Counsel on IRIS-KS flare in the first 2-3 months after ART initiation or switch (worsening edema, new nodules, airway or GI symptoms); distinguish flare from true progression before escalating to systemic chemotherapy.
Escalate to the advanced-disease systemic pathway for increasing lesion burden, new edema, ulceration, or any visceral symptom.

nodes.name: HIV-KS Advanced Treatment
nodes.title: HIV-KS, Advanced: ART Plus Liposomal Doxorubicin (Category 1 Preferred)
nodes.description: ART optimization plus frontline systemic chemotherapy for symptomatic, widespread, edematous, or visceral HIV-associated KS.
bullets: Optimize ART in parallel with chemotherapy for every patient (initiate immediately if naive; resistance-test and switch if viremic); never delay ART for chemotherapy and never delay chemotherapy for ART response when visceral or rapidly progressive disease is present.

Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 2-3 weeks (Category 1 preferred): indicated for symptomatic, widespread, edematous, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, or rapidly progressive disease; continue to maximal response plus 2 consolidation cycles, then stop and observe on ART.

Weekly paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 IV every 2 weeks (Category 1 preferred alternative): use for anthracycline contraindication (cardiac dysfunction, prior anthracycline maximum), patient preference, or access constraints; premedicate per taxane protocol and monitor neuropathy.

Pulmonary KS specifics: coordinate bronchoscopy findings with oncology and pulmonology; avoid diagnostic delay for hemoptysis or airway compromise; corticosteroids may flare KS, so use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration when airway edema mandates them.

Response assessment every 2-3 cycles: lesion photography, edema and pain scores, chest imaging for pulmonary disease, endoscopy only for initially involved symptomatic GI sites, CD4 and viral load trends; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses from the referenced protocol.

nodes.name: HIV-KS Refractory Treatment
nodes.title: HIV-KS, Refractory: Second-Line Systemic Therapy
nodes.description: Second-line and refractory options after progression on frontline liposomal anthracycline with optimized ART.
bullets: Weekly paclitaxel (Category 1 for anthracycline-refractory disease): preferred second-line after liposomal doxorubicin failure when not used frontline; monitor cumulative neuropathy, neutropenia, and hypersensitivity.

Pomalidomide 5 mg orally once daily on days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle: immunomodulatory option with demonstrated KS activity including in ART-controlled disease; thromboprophylaxis assessment, CBC monitoring, and strict pregnancy prevention required.
Lenalidomide: immunomodulatory alternative where pomalidomide is unavailable or intolerable, with the same thrombotic, hematologic, and teratogenicity precautions.
Gemcitabine: cytotoxic option for taxane- and anthracycline-exposed disease or when immunomodulatory agents are unsuitable; monitor myelosuppression, transaminitis, and pulmonary toxicity.

Before switching lines, confirm true progression (versus IRIS-KS flare), verify ART adherence and viral suppression, re-biopsy atypical or rapidly changing lesions, re-screen for MCD/KICS, and offer clinical trial enrollment at every refractory step.

nodes.name: Classic KS Extent
nodes.title: Classic / Mediterranean KS: Disease Extent
nodes.description: Stratify classic KS by cutaneous burden, symptoms, edema control, and visceral spread. Indolent limited disease stays local; extensive or visceral disease needs systemic therapy.
bullets: Limited disease: few patches or plaques confined to the lower extremities, minimal or compression-controlled edema, no ulceration, bleeding, pain, or functional impairment, and no visceral involvement.

Extensive or symptomatic disease: numerous or confluent plaques and nodules, progressive or refractory lymphedema, ulcerated or bleeding lesions, pain or gait limitation, rapid tempo, lymph node involvement, or any visceral spread.
Stage with contrast CT of involved regions and chest imaging when symptoms or extensive disease raise visceral concern; endoscopy or bronchoscopy only for localizing symptoms.

options.label: Limited: few lower-extremity lesions, controlled edema, no visceral disease
Extensive or symptomatic: confluent, ulcerated, edematous, or visceral disease

nodes.name: Classic KS Limited Treatment
nodes.title: Classic KS, Limited: Local Therapy or Observation
nodes.description: Limited classic KS is managed locally or observed; systemic therapy is reserved for progression to extensive disease.
bullets: Observation is appropriate for asymptomatic, stable, cosmetically acceptable lesions; examine skin, edema, and function every 3-6 months with serial photography.

Low-dose radiotherapy 20-30 Gy to symptomatic or cosmetically distressing plaques and nodules: high local response rates in classic KS; use electrons or photons with bolus per lesion depth and shield uninvolved skin.
Graduated compression stockings plus leg elevation, physiotherapy, and dermatologic skin care for chronic lymphedema and stasis changes of the lower extremities.
Intralesional vinblastine, topical alitretinoin 0.1% gel, or surgical excision for isolated painful, bleeding, or ulcerated nodules.
Escalate to systemic therapy for confluent spread beyond radiation fields, refractory edema, ulceration, functional loss, rapid tempo, or visceral involvement.

nodes.name: Classic KS Advanced Treatment
nodes.title: Classic KS, Extensive: Systemic Liposomal Doxorubicin or Paclitaxel
nodes.description: Systemic chemotherapy for extensive, symptomatic, rapidly progressive, or visceral classic KS.
bullets: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 2-3 weeks (Category 1 preferred): frontline for extensive cutaneous, edematous, ulcerated, or visceral classic KS; continue to maximal response plus 2 consolidation cycles.

Weekly paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 IV every 2 weeks (Category 1 preferred alternative): use for anthracycline contraindication, cardiac comorbidity common in this elderly population, or prior anthracycline exposure; baseline cardiac assessment before anthracycline initiation.
Palliative radiotherapy to dominant painful, bleeding, or obstructive lesions may continue alongside systemic therapy for symptom control.

Response assessment every 2-3 cycles with lesion photography, edema and pain scores, and cross-sectional imaging of initially involved visceral sites; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses from the referenced protocol.

nodes.name: Endemic KS Extent
nodes.title: Endemic / African KS: Disease Pattern
nodes.description: Separate indolent cutaneous endemic KS, managed locally, from aggressive lymphadenopathic or visceral disease, which needs systemic chemotherapy.
bullets: Indolent cutaneous pattern: limited patches, plaques, or nodules without bulky lymphadenopathy, edema, ulceration, or visceral symptoms; chronic stable course.

Aggressive pattern: bulky or generalized lymphadenopathy (including florid lymphadenopathic disease in children), extensive or fungating skin disease, tumor-associated edema, or pulmonary/gastrointestinal visceral involvement.
Confirm HIV-negative status (HIV-1/2 serology) to hold the endemic classification; a positive result re-routes the patient to the epidemic pathway. Screen for MCD/KICS in aggressive presentations.

options.label: Indolent cutaneous disease without nodal bulk or visceral spread
Aggressive: bulky lymphadenopathic, fungating, edematous, or visceral disease

nodes.name: Endemic KS Indolent Treatment
nodes.title: Endemic KS, Indolent: Local Therapy
nodes.description: Indolent cutaneous endemic KS is managed with local measures; systemic therapy is reserved for progression.
bullets: Low-dose radiotherapy 20-30 Gy to symptomatic or cosmetically distressing lesions; single-fraction or hypofractionated schedules where radiotherapy access is limited.
Intralesional vinblastine, topical alitretinoin 0.1% gel, or surgical excision for isolated nodules; compression and elevation for lymphedema.
Observe stable asymptomatic lesions with regular skin, nodal, and symptom review; photograph sentinel lesions to detect tempo change early.
Escalate to systemic chemotherapy for nodal bulk, fungating spread, refractory edema, ulceration, functional loss, or any visceral symptom.

nodes.name: Endemic KS Aggressive Treatment
nodes.title: Endemic KS, Aggressive: Systemic Chemotherapy
nodes.description: Systemic chemotherapy for lymphadenopathic, fungating, edematous, or visceral endemic KS.
bullets: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 2-3 weeks (Category 1 preferred): frontline for bulky nodal, visceral, or rapidly progressive endemic KS; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses from the referenced protocol.
Weekly paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 IV every 2 weeks (Category 1 preferred alternative): use for anthracycline contraindication or access constraints; premedicate per taxane protocol.
Etoposide (oral or intravenous): alternative where anthracyclines and taxanes are unavailable, unsuitable, or previously exhausted; monitor myelosuppression and gastrointestinal tolerance.
Pediatric lymphadenopathic endemic KS: involve pediatric oncology; prioritize anthracycline-based therapy with late-effect (cardiac, fertility) counseling and long-term follow-up.
Response assessment every 2-3 cycles with nodal measurements, lesion photography, edema scores, and imaging of initially involved visceral sites.

nodes.name: Iatrogenic KS Management
nodes.title: Iatrogenic / Transplant-Associated KS: Management Track
nodes.description: Decide between immunosuppression taper with mTOR conversion for controllable disease and upfront systemic chemotherapy for visceral or life-threatening KS, always jointly with the transplant team.
bullets: Taper track: limited cutaneous or mucosal disease without visceral involvement, where graft function permits calcineurin inhibitor reduction and mTOR inhibitor conversion with close rejection surveillance.

Systemic-chemotherapy track: pulmonary or gastrointestinal visceral involvement, bulky or rapidly progressive disease, ulcerated or bleeding lesions unresponsive to taper, or any life-threatening presentation.
Every decision is co-made with the transplant team; document graft type, baseline function, rejection history, and the agreed immunosuppression floor before any change.

options.label: Controllable disease: taper immunosuppression and convert to mTOR inhibitor
Visceral, life-threatening, or taper-refractory disease: systemic chemotherapy

nodes.name: Iatrogenic KS Taper Treatment
nodes.title: Iatrogenic KS: Reduce Immunosuppression, Convert to mTOR Inhibitor
nodes.description: Immunosuppression manipulation is first therapy for controllable iatrogenic KS, with local therapy for residual lesions.
bullets: Taper calcineurin inhibitors (cyclosporine, tacrolimus) to the lowest graft-safe level and reduce or withdraw corticosteroids where feasible; every step is directed jointly with the transplant team with graft-function and drug-level monitoring.

Convert to an mTOR inhibitor (sirolimus or everolimus), which provides dual immunosuppressive and anti-KS antineoplastic activity; monitor mTOR drug levels, lipids, proteinuria, cytopenias, and wound healing.
Add local therapy for residual or bothersome lesions: low-dose radiotherapy 20-30 Gy, intralesional vinblastine, topical alitretinoin 0.1% gel, or excision of isolated nodules.
Reassess skin, mucosa, graft function, and drug levels every 2-4 weeks; regression typically begins within weeks to months of conversion.
Escalate to systemic chemotherapy for new visceral symptoms, bulky progression, or failure to regress after 3 months of optimized taper and conversion.

nodes.name: Iatrogenic KS Systemic Treatment
nodes.title: Iatrogenic KS, Visceral: Systemic Liposomal Doxorubicin
nodes.description: Systemic chemotherapy alongside graft-safe immunosuppression adjustment for visceral, life-threatening, or taper-refractory iatrogenic KS.
bullets: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 2-3 weeks (Category 1 preferred): frontline for visceral, bulky, bleeding, or life-threatening iatrogenic KS; continue to maximal response plus 2 consolidation cycles.

Reduce calcineurin inhibitor exposure and convert toward mTOR inhibition in parallel wherever graft function permits; coordinate chemotherapy timing with transplant nephrology or hepatology and monitor graft function each cycle.
Weekly paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 IV every 2 weeks is the Category 1 preferred alternative for anthracycline contraindication or intolerance.

Response assessment every 2-3 cycles with lesion photography, edema scores, graft-function labs, mTOR/calcineurin drug levels, and imaging of initially involved visceral sites; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses from the referenced protocol.
